subject: Post-call recap: connection fanout, concurrency targets & ratecard next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbushq.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: connection fanout, concurrency targets & ratecard next steps

Hi Sophie — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance and quota expectations.

Key items you shared (please correct if I misremember):
- Latency goal: 95th < 100ms for single-request generation (most user journeys)
- Sustained throughput: ~1,000 req/s average; expected short bursts to ~2,000 req/s for 20-40s
- Concurrent parallel requests: steady-state ~800; peak concurrency up to ~1,200
- Streaming sessions: long-lived streams for chat/video captions, ~150 concurrent typical, up to 300 in peak windows; average generation per stream ~5-10 tokens/s
- Typical response body size: 0.5–1.5 MB for multimodal-enriched text chunks
- Retry behavior: client will implement 3 retries with exponential backoff; want guidance on idempotency keys and recommended retry windows
- Connection preferences: prefer HTTP/2 with multiplexing where possible; connection pooling and keepalives are critical to avoid TCP churn

Notes on constraints and options from Redwood:
- Our hosted defaults include per-account rate limits that protect shared pools. We can open a temporary, scoped increase to match the burst/concurrency shape for a PoC, but sustained production at the numbers above is usually handled by Dedicated (reserved capacity) to guarantee SLOs and predictable cost.
- Streaming: we support long-lived HTTP/2 streams and SSE; very high counts (hundreds) are feasible but require capacity sizing and tuned LVUs (long-lived connection units) in Dedicated or a temporary quota bump on Hosted with monitoring hooks.

Attachments: I attached a quick connection profile template (nimbus_conn_profile.xlsx) — please fill in your traffic shape and token size distribution and send back. I also attached a draft ratecard so we have a starting point for pricing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie: send the filled connection profile + traffic replay sample (we can work from a week of traffic or a synthetic replay).
2) Redwood: Marcus to run a capacity estimate and confirm whether we can grant a hosted soft-limit increase for a 2–4 week PoC and what that increase looks like (numbers below).
3) Technical sync: schedule a 60-minute infra sync (recommend early next week) to validate connection settings (HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1, keepalive timeouts, max concurrent streams).
4) Commercial: Lauren to prepare an initial PoC quote and temporary rate-limit proposal; Sophie to confirm procurement timeline.

Tentative temporary limits we should discuss (PoC, subject to final sizing):
- Sustained: 1,000 req/s (with short bursts to 2,000 req/s limited to 30s windows)
- Parallel connections: 1,200 concurrent requests (client-side concurrent HTTP requests)
- Streaming: 300 concurrent long-lived streams
- Token throughput: estimated 10,000 tokens/sec aggregated across streams during peak

If those numbers look off, tell me where to correct. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbushq.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@nimbushq.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: connection fanout, concurrency targets & ratecard next steps

Thanks Ben — this is a good summary and mostly aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Burst profile: we can hit ~2k req/s but usually for 20-40s during peak user events.
- Streaming: average tokens/stream is closer to 8 tokens/s during active typing windows; idle streams are common (open for minutes with sparse traffic).
- Connection limits: our infra prefers fewer long-lived connections with multiplexing to reduce NAT table churn; if Redwood supports HTTP/2 streams multiplexed over fewer sockets that's ideal.
- Failover: we need a clearly defined fallback policy if the hosted pool rate-limits us mid-session (e.g., degrade to lower-quality model or queue messages).

We attached a small synthetic traffic sample (nimbus-traffic-shape.json) to help with sizing.

Commercial asks:
- Can Redwood offer a 30-day PoC with temporary quota increases to the tentative limits you suggested?
- We need an estimated monthly run-rate for the PoC (ballpark is fine) and a rough quote for production if we move to Dedicated capacity.

We can fill the connection profile this afternoon. I’m looping in procurement (separately) but our timeline is tight — would like to kick a PoC by Oct 4.

Best,
Sophie Chen
Head of Platform, NimBus HQ
sophie.chen@nimbushq.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbushq.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: connection fanout, concurrency targets & ratecard next steps

Thanks Sophie — appreciated. Quick replies inline and a concrete proposal so we can move forward: 

Inline:
- Burst windows of ~20–40s at 2k req/s: we can support that for a PoC with a temporary hosted quota increase, provided we have clear burst windows in the replay and a signed PoC agreement to reserve capacity.
- Streaming token rate ~8 t/s: noted. That shapes CPU vs memory sizing and will increase LVU consumption for long-lived sessions.
- HTTP/2 multiplexing: supported and recommended for your pattern; reduces socket counts substantially. We’ll document keepalive/idle time recommendations in the infra sync.
- Fallback policy: we propose automatic model-fallback + graceful throttling (queue 429s with client-side backoff + degrade to smaller model). We’ll draft a recommended fallback config.

Concrete PoC offer (subject to internal approval):
- Duration: 30 days starting once PoC SOW is signed and we receive a traffic sample for replay.
- Temporary hosted increases (soft limits): 2,000 req/s burst cap (30s windows), sustained 1,200 req/s, 1,200 parallel concurrency target, 300 streaming LVUs.
- Instrumentation: Redwood provides streaming telemetry (per-route latency/tokens/cost) and a shared dashboard with your engineers for the PoC.
- Cost indication: ballpark hosted overage + telemetry for PoC: $12k–$20k for the 30-day window depending on token churn and model family. Dedicated (reserved) estimate for production: starting at $20k/mo (smallest pool) — will refine after Marcus runs the capacity model.

Next steps we need from NimBus:
1) Signed PoC SOW (I’ll have Lauren draft an initial one today).
2) Filled connection profile and either a 48-hour traffic replay or the synthetic file you already attached.
3) Technical sync — Marcus, can you run a quick sizing pass today and propose whether the hosted soft-limit increases are acceptable versus recommending Dedicated for immediate production?

I’ve attached a short note with the proposed temporary boost terms (redwood-proposed-temp-boost.pdf). Lauren will follow up on commercial terms.

If Oct 4 is the desired PoC start, we should lock the SOW and traffic replay this week. Happy to run the infra call tomorrow — what time works for Sophie?

—Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: connection fanout, concurrency targets & ratecard next steps

Looping you both for action items and internal approval. Key asks:
- Lauren: draft a 30-day PoC SOW that includes the temporary hosted increases (sustained 1,200 req/s, burst 2k for 30s, 300 LVUs). Include an escape clause for capacity concerns and an acceptance criteria block tied to latency SLOs and error rates.
- Marcus: run capacity-sizing using the attached synthetic sample (nimbus-traffic-shape.json) and confirm whether we can safely grant the hosted soft-limit increases for a 30-day PoC without impacting other customers. If not, recommend the minimal Dedicated pool configuration and a delta cost estimate.

Risk notes: if we increase hosted quotas without reservation we run risk of noisy neighbor effects. If we suggest Dedicated, include migration steps and timeline so Sophie can see the path to production.

Please reply with status and I’ll coordinate with Sophie to lock dates.

Thanks —
Ben
